clue.text: Team including daughter in matches or some athletics

indicators.note: the team-with-daughter piece sits inside the word for matches

parts.note: to match is to fit, so matches gives fits

indicators.note: the team takes the daughter's letter into its middle

parts.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven

explanation.surface: A team with a daughter on its roster takes part in matches or some athletics events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team' reads as a sports side here, a cricket or football eleven; 'including' and 'in' are the two container signals, giving ELDEVEN within the matches word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping and throwing contests at an athletics meeting are collectively the field events, as opposed to track races.

clue.text: Book with poem shown up as minor piece of fiction

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A book with a poem in it exposed as a slight piece of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' turns B + IF round. IF is Rudyard Kipling's well-known poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A small untruth is a little made-up story, a minor fiction told to deceive.

clue.text: European state, after second attempt

indicators.note: the word for state follows the letter for second

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: A European country makes a second attempt at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To try something is to make an attempt at it, an older sense of the word as a noun.

clue.text: Make number difficult for Cockney simpleton

parts.note: number here is more numb; to dull is to make numb
difficult is hard, which a Cockney says dropping the H

explanation.surface: Making a number tricky for a Londoner who is a bit slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' reads as a figure but means more numb. Cockneys, from East London, drop their Hs, so hard becomes 'ard.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-witted, stupid person is a dullard, a synonym for a simpleton.

clue.text: Churchman promises to pay for what's second-hand

parts.note: a vicar is a parish priest in the Church of England
IOUs (I owe you) are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A clergyman pledges to pay for goods bought used.
explanation.definitionFit: Experience felt through another person rather than first-hand is vicarious, so second-hand in that sense.

clue.text: Pressman finally privy to delicate material

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of the word pressman

parts.note: to be privy to a secret is to be in on it

explanation.surface: A journalist ultimately gets to know about some fine fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer fabric of silk or nylon, used for dresses and curtains.

clue.text: Author getting royalty relatively fast

parts.note: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A writer receives royalties comparatively quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royalty' looks like a writer's earnings but means the monarch, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative form of a word for speedy means faster than something else, so relatively fast.

clue.text: Gilbert and Sullivan primarily something that's entertaining

indicators.note: primarily takes the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Gilbert and Sullivan operas are, above all, good fun.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech a gas is a lot of fun, something highly enjoyable.

clue.text: Contents of scoop from China, perhaps — explosive stuff

definitions.text: Contents of scoop from China, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a Chinese green tea rolled into pellets is named after the black powder it resembles
the black powder used in early firearms and fireworks

explanation.walkthrough: Gunpowder tea, from China, is rolled into small pellets that look like the explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a tightly rolled Chinese green tea and the black explosive mix of saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal.

clue.text: Beginning something new that's repeatedly not working

parts.note: workers on strike are striking, not working
a machine that is out is not working

explanation.surface: Starting afresh by being out of work over and over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' tells you to use 'not working' twice, for two different words.
explanation.definitionFit: To head off independently on a new venture is the idiom striking out, setting off afresh.

clue.text: Like court in Rome assigning prison after bail is misused

indicators.note: the word for prison comes after the rearranged letters
the letters of the two words are used wrongly, so rearranged

parts.note: can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A Roman court sentences someone to jail after bail is abused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges BAILIS to BASILI.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica was a Roman hall of justice, so basilican describes something like that court building.

clue.text: Not a bad shot, private

definitions.meaning: in archery or shooting, the ring next to the bullseye scores well
personal and hidden, as in one's private thoughts

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the ring just outside a target's bull, a decent hit, and also means intimate or personal.

clue.text: Prosperous part of our capital market after part of year

indicators.note: the word for market follows the month

parts.note: May is a month, part of the year
a fair is a market or trade show

explanation.surface: A wealthy district of London holds a market after part of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an upmarket district of central London; 'our capital' assumes a British reader.
explanation.definitionFit: This expensive West End district is a well-known wealthy area of London, the capital meant.

clue.text: It's held up by dreadful mischance, subject to physical processes

indicators.note: the reversed word is held inside the rearranged letters
dreadful signals that the letters of mischance are in a dreadful mess
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the word it, with 's as is

explanation.surface: It is caught up by a terrible stroke of bad luck, at the mercy of physical forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' makes MECHANISC; 'up' reverses the pronoun and 'held' lodges it before the final C. The 's is simply 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanistic view explains things purely as the working of physical causes, like a machine.

clue.text: Score composition for broadcasting group

parts.note: to score a goal is to net it
a piece of music or writing is a work

explanation.surface: A musical score composed for a broadcasting company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like music beside 'composition', but it is the verb, to net a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of linked television or radio stations is a broadcasting network.

clue.text: Circle line — a sensitive location for strike

definitions.meaning: a straight line joining two points on a circle's edge, in geometry
to strike one is to touch an emotional nerve, as in the idiom

explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route, a misleading surface here. To strike a chord is to make someone feel something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a geometric segment between two points of a circle and what you strike when you move someone.

clue.text: Suitable work on piano with golden melody

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
or is gold in heraldry
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A fitting musical work for piano with a golden melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well timed and appropriate to the moment is opportune, fitting the occasion.

clue.text: Fellow from Exeter, say, has footwear to put on

parts.note: an oxford is a laced leather shoe
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Someone from Exeter wearing shoes he has to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter looks like the Devon city, but Exeter College is part of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is an Oxford college, so its fellows are academics there, called dons.

clue.text: Shell bursting inside military post didn't reach target

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the military post

parts.note: a fort is a fortified military post

indicators.note: a shell bursting breaks apart, so its letters scatter

explanation.surface: A shell exploding within a garrison didn't hit its target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting' makes ELLSH, which 'inside' places within the garrison word; the surface's artillery shell is pure misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall short is to fail to reach a goal or mark, as a missile landing too near.

clue.text: Evaluation bringing shock about extra pay cut

indicators.note: the word for shock goes around the shortened pay rise

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: cut docks the final letter of the word for extra pay

parts.note: a raise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: An assessment that brings a shock about a reduced pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last letter of the pay word, and 'about' wraps the shock word round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is a formal assessment of worth or performance, so an evaluation.

clue.text: A pressure is painful for some Americans

parts.note: p is the symbol for pressure in physics
something that aches is painful

explanation.surface: Pressure hurts some people in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Native American peoples of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Approximately on end of elephant's trunk

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
end of picks only the closing letter of elephant

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: Roughly at the tip of an elephant's trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' looks like the elephant's nose but means the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, without head and limbs, is the torso.

clue.text: Daisy's family member putting revised list in article

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put in the article

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: a revised list has its order changed

explanation.surface: Putting an amended list into an article about a daisy's relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges LIST as ISTL, which goes 'in' THE.
explanation.definitionFit: This prickly plant belongs to the Asteraceae, the botanical family that includes the daisy.

clue.text: Ordered on raids, attacks

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Raids are ordered, the attacks begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a command to attack but rearranges ON RAIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are advances made into enemy territory, hostile incursions or attacks.

clue.text: No fast food for the French?

definitions.text: No fast food for the French?

parts.words: No fast food for the French?
parts.note: the French eat escargots, a dish that is a famously slow creature

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that it is food for the French but no fast mover.
explanation.definitionFit: The French delicacy escargot is a slow-moving garden mollusc, food that is anything but fast.

clue.text: Trim poodle, say, a little bit

parts.note: to snip is to trim with scissors
a poodle is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Trim the poodle just a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment of something.

clue.text: Hollywood creation recently losing status within star system

definitions.text: recently losing status within star system
definitions.meaning: demoted in 2006 from planet to dwarf planet in the solar system

explanation.walkthrough: 'star system' is the solar system, not Hollywood's star system.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Mickey Mouse's cartoon dog and to the body reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

clue.text: Compete with skill

definitions.meaning: to rival, as in nobody can ... her
a deft ... is a light skilled manner

explanation.definitionFit: To be the equal of someone is to come near them in ability; a deft knack is also called this.

clue.text: Major change of attitude on revolution

parts.note: on and about both mean concerning
a revolution is a turn

explanation.surface: A big change of heart on the subject of a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a military drill command to face the opposite way, it now means a complete reversal of opinion.

clue.text: Sign agreement getting new act overturned

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the word is flipped upwards

parts.note: to do is to act

explanation.surface: A signed agreement is overturned by a new law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns DO into OD.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod the head is to signal assent, a gesture that signs agreement.

clue.text: Signal for player to hit ball, in a way

definitions.meaning: the line or prompt telling an actor to come in

definitions.text: to hit ball, in a way
definitions.meaning: to strike a ball with a billiards or snooker stick

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an actor's prompt to speak and also the action of striking a snooker ball with the stick.

clue.text: Go after one for short time

parts.note: split is slang for leave or go
what comes after first is second

explanation.surface: Leave right after someone for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second is an instant, a very brief moment of time.
